Advances: specled.package

Two pre-existing findings surfaced by cold verification of specled_-vk0 (epic specled_-233, 2026-07-26). NEITHER was introduced by that ticket — both reproduce at its base a6954fc9 — so both were correctly left out of it.

FINDING 1 — stale absolute counts in the ADR. .spec/decisions/specled.decision.doc_identifier_lint_spec_corpus.md cites absolute corpus occurrence counts for the four unusable stems as detector_ 69, requirement_ 45, decision_ 24, verification_ 39. Measured 2026-07-26 against the real 97-file corpus: 78, 110, 46, 39. Only verification_ still matches. Guidance-only counting gives 24/24/8/1, which matches neither, so the numbers cannot be recovered by reinterpreting the corpus.

Why it matters and why it is low priority: the ADR's LOAD-BEARING claim is comparative, not absolute — that the four stems collide with real non-code identifiers while the deferred narrow stems (surface_target_, scenario_cover_, meta_field_) collide with nothing. That comparative claim reproduces EXACTLY (5, 11, 12 and 19 distinct non-code collisions respectively; zero occurrences for the deferred stems; spec_requirement_ 12 and invalid_id_ 1, each match being the stem's own real code). So the argument is sound and only its illustrative figures have drifted. Fix: either refresh the four numbers, or reword them as approximations, or drop them and keep the comparative statement — the last is probably best, since absolute counts in an ADR will drift again by construction.

FINDING 2 — mirror union masks a single-file decommission. test/docs_identifier_lint_test.exs's two-way mirror derives the implementation code set as a UNION over the 10 files in @implementation_code_files. Consequence: a code removed from its EMITTING detector while a literal survives elsewhere (typically lib/specled_ex/branch_check.ex @per_code_defaults) keeps the mirror green. Reproduced: replacing "overlap/must_stem_collision" in lib/specled_ex/overlap.ex left all 16 tests GREEN because branch_check.ex:38 still carries the literal. 22 of the 37 guarded codes appear in 2+ listed files and share this seam; the 15 single-occurrence codes are fully covered (confirmed with cross_field/affects_empty, which goes RED reporting 'dead in @known_codes').

Note this is arguably CORRECT union semantics rather than a defect — if branch_check.ex still lists the code in its severity defaults, the code has not actually left the implementation. specled_-vk0's stated failure mode (a code deleted from lib/ entirely) does go RED, so that ticket delivered what it scoped. Only pursue this if the project wants the deletion arm to detect per-detector decommission specifically, which would mean distinguishing 'emitting site' from 'referenced site' rather than unioning them.

ALSO WORTH FIXING WHILE THERE (cheap, cosmetic, from the same verification):
- Stale forward pointers to specled_-vk0 that will dangle once it closes: the moduledoc at test/docs_identifier_lint_test.exs:44 ('Deferred to specled_-vk0, not impossible') and the @token_patterns comment at :155-156 ('tightening the lookbehind bounds is tracked in specled_-vk0'). vk0 correctly declared the surface_target_/scenario_cover_ widening out of scope and did NOT tighten the lookbehind (A3 asked for boundary tests, not a tightening), so both pointers need retargeting or rewording.
- @known_code_list (:139) is dead indirection — introduced and consumed only at :142 to build @known_codes.
- @implementation_code_files is a new hand-maintained 10-file list whose own staleness is unguarded, though it fails loudly in the safe direction.

ADMISSION VERIFICATION (specled_-k6s, 2026-07-27)
Cold fresh-context verifier run against the epic base tree (feat/specled_-td7-self-identifying-descriptors @ e81f9f98).

VERDICT: premise_wrong   EFFORT: small

== MANDATE AS ADMITTED (implement THIS, not the original description) ==
Do NOT use the ticket's numbers (78/110/46/39); they are measured under the wrong grammar. Real work is small:

1. .spec/decisions/specled.decision.doc_identifier_lint_spec_corpus.md:69-71 — the parenthetical is stale by exactly one on two stems. Either (preferred, per the ticket's own recommendation) drop the four absolute figures and the "24-69 times" range, keeping only the comparative claim ("each occurs many times in the scanned corpus, against zero occurrences for surface_target_/scenario_cover_/meta_field_"), OR refresh to `detector_` 70, `requirement_` 46, `verification_` 39, `decision_` 24 and the range "24-70". If refreshing rather than dropping, state the counting rule inline so it stays falsifiable: `(?<![\w/])<stem>[a-z_]+` over skills/**/*.md + docs/**/*.md + README.md + .spec/**/*.md. Leave ADR:61-63 ("nine, four, and six") and ADR:73-75 (0/0/0/12/1) alone — all still measure correctly.

2. test/docs_identifier_lint_test.exs:44 — replace "Deferred to specled_-vk0, not impossible" with a non-dangling formulation (vk0 is closed and explicitly declared the surface_target_/scenario_cover_ widening out of scope). E.g. "Deferred, not impossible".

3. test/docs_identifier_lint_test.exs:155-156 — replace "tightening the lookbehind bounds is tracked in specled_-vk0" with a bare statement of the residual risk and no ticket pointer (vk0 closed without tightening it).

4. test/docs_identifier_lint_test.exs:139-142 — inline @known_code_list into @known_codes: `@known_codes MapSet.new(@append_only_codes ++ @overlap_codes ++ @evidence_codes ++ @cross_field_codes ++ @branch_guard_codes)` and delete the @known_code_list attribute (no other reference exists in the repo).

5. If the ADR moduledoc mirror at test/docs_identifier_lint_test.exs:20-33 is touched, note it carries no absolute occurrence counts (only the nine/four/six distinct-identifier figures, all still correct) — leave it.

EXPLICITLY OUT OF SCOPE unless the orchestrator decides otherwise: FINDING 2 (union → per-emitting-site distinction in implementation_guarded_codes/0) and guarding @implementation_code_files staleness. The ticket itself scopes both as optional and both are non-defects under the current contract.

== EVIDENCE ==
TICKET'S CENTRAL QUANTITATIVE CLAIM IS FALSE IN THIS TREE.

The ADR text under attack is intact at .spec/decisions/specled.decision.doc_identifier_lint_spec_corpus.md:69-71:
  "The must calls those four \"heavily-referenced\", on this basis: each occurs
   24-69 times in the scanned corpus (`detector_` 69, `requirement_` 45,
   `verification_` 39, `decision_` 24), against zero collisions for every"

The ticket asserts (a) measured values are "78, 110, 46, 39", (b) "Only verification_ still matches", (c) "the numbers cannot be recovered by reinterpreting the corpus". All three are wrong.

The ADR itself fixes the counting rule: corpus = skills/**/*.md + docs/**/*.md + README.md + .spec/**/*.md (ADR:39-40), token grammar = the lint's own `(?<![\w/])<stem>[a-z_]+` (ADR:106-109; restated in test/docs_identifier_lint_test.exs:49-51 "`(?<![\w/])requirement_` cannot match mid-token"). Measured with exactly that rule:

  at c13d1bdd (the commit that INTRODUCED the numbers, found via `git log -S'`detector_` 69'`):
    detector_=69  requirement_=45  decision_=24  verification_=39   → all four EXACT
  at a6954fc9 (vk0's base, where the ticket claims to reproduce):
    detector_=70  requirement_=45  decision_=24  verification_=39   → three exact
  at HEAD (d407f482):
    detector_=70  requirement_=46  decision_=24  verification_=39   → two exact, two off by ONE

So the counting rule is fully recoverable and was exact when authored; real drift is +1 on detector_ and +1 on requirement_, not the 9-to-65 gaps the ticket reports. The ticket's 78/110/46/39 reproduce only when the lookbehind is dropped (`rg -o "requirement_[a-z_]+"` gives 125 at HEAD, 78 for detector_) — i.e. by counting `spec_requirement_` as a `requirement_` hit, which is precisely the conflation ADR:104-105 and test:47-52 exist to warn against.

Corroboration that the rule is the right one: the same paragraph's secondary figures at ADR:73-75 all still measure EXACT at HEAD under it — surface_target_=0, scenario_cover_=0, meta_field_=0, spec_requirement_=12, invalid_id_=1. Likewise ADR:61-63 "`decision_` ... nine ... `requirement_` ... six": distinct decision_* identifiers in corpus = 9 (decision_deleted, decision_governance, decision_index, decision_fork_loop_line, decision_fork_guidance, decision_new_scaffold, decision_fork_advertised_at_decision_points, decision_dir, decision_file_deleted); distinct requirement_* non-codes (no string literal in lib/) = 6 (requirement_deleted, requirement_deleted_authorized, requirement_override, requirement_override_replaces_tier, requirement_without_tag_emits_finding, requirement_id).

Drift sources are identifiable: detector_ +1 = .spec/specs/package.spec.md detector_unavailable 2→3; requirement_ +1 = .spec/specs/spec_review.spec.md requirement_id 1→2.

FINDING 2 — TRUE AS STATED, BUT SELF-DESCOPED. test/docs_identifier_lint_test.exs:532-545 `implementation_guarded_codes/0` still `Enum.flat_map`s @implementation_code_files (:184-195, 10 files) into one MapSet, and :357-364 compares that union to @known_codes. The named seam is real: lib/specled_ex/branch_check.ex:38 `"overlap/must_stem_collision" => :error` co-exists with lib/specled_ex/overlap.ex:125 `code: "overlap/must_stem_collision"`. The ticket itself declines the fix: "arguably CORRECT union semantics rather than a defect ... Only pursue this if the project wants the deletion arm to detect per-detector decommission specifically."

COSMETIC ITEMS — ALL FOUR STILL PRESENT VERBATIM AT THE CITED LINES:
- test/docs_identifier_lint_test.exs:44 "Deferred to specled_-vk0, not impossible"
- test/docs_identifier_lint_test.exs:155-156 "No such reference exists today; tightening the lookbehind / bounds is tracked in specled_-vk0."
- `bw show specled_-vk0` → "✓ specled_-vk0" (CLOSED), so both pointers now dangle exactly as predicted.
- :139 `@known_code_list` is consumed only at :142 `@known_codes MapSet.new(@known_code_list)`; repo-wide grep returns only those two lines.
- :184-195 @implementation_code_files is the unguarded hand-maintained 10-file list.

The must at .spec/specs/package.spec.md:112-115 carries NO absolute counts — only the word "heavily-referenced" — so no spec requirement text needs to change.

== RISK NOTES ==
REALIZATION HASH: no risk. grep of .spec/realization_hashes.json for "doc_identifier"/"docs_identifier" returns nothing; specled.package.doc_identifier_integrity has no realized_by binding to the lint test (package.spec.md realized_by at :63-69 lists only SpecLedEx public API functions). Change is ADR prose + test comments + one dead module attribute — no lib/ edit, so no drift.

SPEC REQUIREMENT: no spec file edit needed. .spec/specs/package.spec.md:112-115 (specled.package.doc_identifier_integrity) contains no absolute counts, only "four heavily-referenced stems". This keeps 4pl OUT of the package.spec.md contention zone that other tickets in the set may occupy.

FILE CONFLICT: specled_-ozm edits the SAME file, test/docs_identifier_lint_test.exs — its regions are @allow_marker_pattern/@allow_marker_comment_pattern (:167-168) and stale_allow_marker_violations_for_line/3 (:492-520). 4pl's nearest edit is the @token_patterns comment at :155-156, ~11 lines above ozm's :167-168 — likely no textual git conflict but inside each other's diff context. Land one, then rebase the other; and note that BOTH tickets' cited line numbers shift once either applies. specled_-yds only CITES docs_identifier_lint_test.exs:298 as precedent and edits a different content-lint test file; conflict is informational only.

SELF-REFERENCE HAZARD (verified benign): editing the ADR does not perturb the numbers it reports. The parenthetical writes the stems backtick-terminated (``detector_` 69`), and the grammar requires `[a-z_]+` after the stem, so those mentions never match. This ADR file contributes exactly 2 detector_ matches (detector_unavailable_by_leg, detector_unavailable at :61 and elsewhere) and 1 decision_ match (decision_deleted at :63) both before and after any numeric edit. A refreshed number therefore stays correct at commit time.

ORDERING: no dependency on any other ticket. specled_-vk0 is already closed, which is what makes the dangling-pointer half of this ticket live rather than premature.

GATE: `mix spec.check --no-run-commands` is sufficient to validate; the ADR body edit touches neither frontmatter (status/affects/change_type unchanged) nor a requirement, so append_only and cross_field detectors are not implicated. The doc-identifier lint itself (16 tests) must stay green — the ADR's two `<!-- spec-lint:allow-code=... -->` markers at :22 and :24 must not be disturbed, or the stale-allow-marker sweep at :423-429 goes red.

SCOPE CONTRACT (orchestrator, specled_-k6s — 2026-07-27)

Authoritative for mechanical scope checks. Supplements, does not replace, the
ADMISSION VERIFICATION comment's mandate — and that comment SUPERSEDES this
ticket's description, which carries measured numbers the admission pass proved
false. Implement the five admitted items, not the description.

## Allowed touches
- `.spec/decisions/specled.decision.doc_identifier_lint_spec_corpus.md` — body
  prose only. Do NOT disturb the two `<!-- spec-lint:allow-code=... -->` markers
  (around lines 22 and 24); the stale-allow-marker sweep goes red if you do.
  Do NOT edit the `affects:` frontmatter list.
- `test/docs_identifier_lint_test.exs`
- `.spec/specs/package.spec.md` — spec co-change is AUTHORIZED, and takes
  precedence over Out of Scope, when the repo's spec gate demands it. Admission
  found no spec edit necessary, so touching this file is an exception you must
  justify in the completion record.

## Out of Scope (files)
- `CHANGELOG.md` — the orchestrator consolidates the 0.11.0 section once at the
  end. Do not append.
- `VERSION`, `.spec/realization_hashes.json`, `.spec/state.json`.
  A realization-hash diff is a red flag: stop and report; never regenerate.
- `lib/**` — this ticket changes no implementation.
- Every file not listed under Allowed touches.

## Out of Scope (intent)
- FINDING 2 (union -> per-emitting-site distinction in
  `implementation_guarded_codes/0`) is EXPLICITLY DESCOPED. Do not implement it.
- Guarding `@implementation_code_files` staleness is EXPLICITLY DESCOPED.
- No new dependencies; `mix.exs` / `mix.lock` unchanged.
- No opportunistic refactors beyond the named `@known_code_list` inlining.
- Do not weaken spec prose or add a false `decisions:` link to quiet
  branch-guard. Use a `Spec-Drift:` commit trailer.

## Verification (change-scoped, run-until-green; host mix, no compose)
1. `mix compile --warnings-as-errors`
2. `mix test test/docs_identifier_lint_test.exs` — all 16 must stay green.
3. `mix spec.check --no-run-commands`

If you refresh the four absolute counts rather than dropping them, you must
state the counting rule inline in the ADR and show the command you measured
with in your completion record. Numbers with no stated counting rule are the
exact defect this ticket exists to fix.

Do NOT run bare `mix spec.check` and do NOT run the full suite.
